summary: Edge proxy header mangling prevents ephemeral token exchange for Runbook UI
description:
Issue summary: Support team received multiple reports that the internal Runbook UI fails to acquire ephemeral session tokens (401) for a subset of users. Impact: Engineers cannot open elevated runbooks via the console, blocking on-call remediation for some incidents. Environment: prod (us-west) via edge-proxy v5.2.2.

Observed behavior: Runbook UI shows 'Unable to fetch ephemeral token' error and support logs surface 401 from identity-service with reason 'missing-subject-claim'. Older sessions (created before 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC) continue to work. New sessions started after an edge-proxy upgrade fail intermittently based on request size and cookie payload.

Required: identify root cause, provide mitigation for oncall, and deploy fix with post-deploy validation and monitoring.
impact: Partial customer/internal outage for runbook elevation flow in prod-us-west; affects oncall ability to execute privileged runbooks for ~4% of attempts. Time-to-fix is critical during active incidents.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to console (okta SSO) in us-west via edge-proxy route
2) Open Runbook UI > request ephemeral session > click 'Acquire Token'
3) Observe spinner then 401 with 'Unable to fetch ephemeral token' and no token in response
4) Reproduce more reliably by adding a long user-agent or large session cookie (>2KB) to HTTP request headers
5) Confirm identity-service audit log shows request missing 'sub' (subject) claim for affected attempts
logs: 2026-03-10T18:14:02Z edge-proxy[router]: downstream request headers truncated for session cookie (size 2279) -> forward without 'x-okta-subject'
2026-03-10T18:14:03Z identity-service[auth]: incoming token-exchange request missing-subject-claim -> reject 401, trace_id=trace-7c3b
2026-03-10T18:14:03Z runbook-service[ui]: tokenExchange failed status=401 reason=missing-subject-claim trace=trace-7c3b
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: RBAC or Okta assertion transform dropped subject when request headers exceeded buffer limits
Reproduced in staging by toggling req header size to >2KB; nginx-like sidecar returned requests with 'x-okta-subject' header missing
Edge-proxy v5.2.2 rolled out 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC included a change to header-buffer-size and gzip header handling from upstream dependency
Correlation: affected users had either long cookie payloads (multiple org sessions) or extended user-agent strings from corporate SSO extensions

Confirmed root cause: proxy upstream (libedge v2.8) introduced a bug where combined header length > configured buffer caused select headers (x-okta-*) to be dropped rather than preserving ordering; identity-service treats missing header as absent subject claim
Reproduction: curl with custom Cookie header length 2300 and observe header dropped on proxy; artifact confirmed with tcpdump on sidecar
actions_taken: 1) Short-term mitigation (2026-03-10 19:10 UTC): traffic for runbook route in us-west rerouted to previous control-plane edge (v5.1.9) via traffic-director -> restored majority of flows
2) Created patch for edge-proxy configuration to increase proxy_buffer_size and enable header-preserve-mode in libedge (PR submitted)
3) Added CI test in edge-proxy that rejects changes which drop x-okta-* headers when combined header length increases
4) Notified SRE and Identity teams and opened rollback playbook for immediate rollback if regression observed
5) Provided users workaround: use CLI token flow (support-runbook-cli) or shorten cookie by logging out other sessions as temporary workaround
resolution: Rollback of libedge upgrade to v5.1.9 on prod-us-west restored normal behavior at 2026-03-10 19:30 UTC. Patch to libedge (fix and config) merged in github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/8721 and deployed to canary; after validation deployed to prod-us-west on 2026-03-12 04:20 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring for 72 hours shows no recurrence. Follow-up: add synthetic test covering large header payloads to CI and add alerting when identity-service sees >0.5% missing-subject-claim errors in a 5m window.
comments: Support (Aisha): Received 6 reports from oncall teams between 18:10-18:25 UTC. All failures returned missing-subject-claim. Escalated to SRE.
SRE (Diego): Identified edge-proxy rollout at 18:00 as common factor, started rollback and traffic re-route. Created canary with increased proxy_buffer_size.
Identity (Lena Zhou): Identity service will add defensive check to map subject from jwt cookie if header absent as a stopgap; this requires security review.
Diego: Patch merged and promoted to canary; post-canary we scheduled prod rollout at 04:20 UTC with 15-min verification windows. No further errors observed after rollout.
